audit.whatIsWrong: The lane-difficulty story was built on a Lillia who dashes twice. Nothing in her kit dashes, so the stated reason the lane is hard is fictional.
audit.why: Riot's text gives Lillia Dream-Laden Bough (P, max-health damage over time), Blooming Blows (Q, 450 range, stacking move speed, true damage on the edge), Watch Out! Eep! (W, 500-range area slam), Swirlseed (E, 700-range rolling projectile that slows) and Lilting Lullaby (R, 1600 range). There is no dash, no shield and no heal anywhere in it. The lane is hard because she kites on Q's move-speed stacks and burns max health, not because she bounces out of melee.
audit.corrected: Rewrote early, mid, late, whys[1], whys[2] and the wants rows around move-speed kiting and Dream-Laden Bough burn, and stated plainly that Lillia owns no dash at any level.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Levels 4-5 line said 'your ability cooldowns are longest' without a single number, and the spike text credited Lillia with 'W dash and second-spin E mobility' she does not have.
audit.why: The real numbers gate the phase: Lacerate is 13/12/11/10/9 and Repudiation 18/17/16/15/14, so at rank 1 Ambessa's re-engage is a 13-second wait. On Lillia's side Swirlseed is a flat 12 seconds at every rank and Watch Out! Eep! is 14 at rank 1 — those are the two windows worth counting.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns now appear in mid, whys[3], spikes[0].text and wants.you[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: Lilting Lullaby's precondition is absent everywhere, and it is the single interaction that decides whether her ultimate exists in this matchup.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Lillia causes all enemies with Dream Dust on them to become Drowsy before falling asleep.' Dream Dust comes from Dream-Laden Bough, which lands only when one of her skills hits you. An unhit Ambessa cannot be slept from 1600 range — the old text treated the sleep as unconditional.
audit.corrected: Stated in late and whys[4]; the drowsy-then-sleep ordering is what gives you time to walk out.
sources: champ-data/_kits/lillia.json (P Dream-Laden Bough, R Lilting Lullaby)

audit.whatIsWrong: Public Execution was described as blinking you 'behind' the farthest enemy.
audit.why: Riot's text: she 'blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line of her choosing and suppresses them upon her arrival.' The word that matters is champion — minions and the wave are irrelevant to where it puts you, and in a 2v2 it will pass Lillia for whoever stands deeper.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text and mid now say 'to the farthest champion in your line'.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole entry told the player to trade 'when Blooming Blows is down'. It is never down.
audit.why: Blooming Blows is 6/5.5/5/4.5/4 seconds. Waiting it out is not a plan. Swirlseed is the punishable cooldown at a flat 12 seconds regardless of rank, and it is the only thing in her kit that can stop you walking at her.
audit.corrected: early, whys[0] and wants.you[1] now point the player at Swirlseed's 12 seconds instead of Q's 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: The text told the player armour-stacking Lillia was a scaling problem but never mentioned that her poke ignores resistances.
audit.why: Blooming Blows deals extra true damage on the edge, and Dream-Laden Bough is max-health damage over time. Neither is reduced by MR. Buying magic resist against her chip reads the trade wrong.
audit.corrected: Threaded into wants.foe[1] and whys[0] rather than written as a standalone itemisation line.

audit.why: Swirlseed's kit entry carries a 'terrain — creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes' flag. Riot's own description says only that the seed keeps rolling until it hits a wall or a target. The flag contradicts the description, so I did not claim Swirlseed can wall off your dash.

edits.before: Lillia is a weak early laner and you can press it, but only by making her stand still. Your opener is landing the Q cone and its Sundering Slam follow-up behind a Lacerate slow so she cannot W-dash or E-bounce away while your empowered auto and Q2 land. Do not throw Q at empty air chasing her movement; bait her W dodge, then commit E first to glue her, because her near-total slow is what turns your short combo from a whiff into a kill threat. At level 1 you are both weak and she has no real escape until W is online, so deny her last-hits and set the lane up for your 2-3 pin.
edits.after: Lillia is a weak early laner and you can press it, but only by making her stand still. Your opener is landing the Q cone and its Sundering Slam follow-up behind a Lacerate slow: she owns no dash at any level, so a slowed Lillia can only walk while your empowered auto and Q2 land. Do not throw Q at empty air chasing her movement; commit E first to glue her, because the slow is what turns your short combo from a whiff into a kill threat. Never wait out Blooming Blows — it is back in 6s at rank 1. Swirlseed is the cooldown that matters, a flat 12s at every rank.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your soft spot: your ability cooldowns are longest, she kites the gaps with W speed and her bouncing E, and she chip-heals off her passive burn and W shield-slam — concede a little and farm toward 6. Then 6 flips it back. Public Execution blinks you behind the farthest enemy in your line (her, in a 1v1) and suppress-stuns straight through her mobility, the one clean answer to a champion built to bounce out of melee. Hold it until her E second-spin dash is spent, then R into Lacerate into Q for the kill. Through first item with Q maxed you out-trade her short combos hard.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your soft spot: Lacerate is 13s and Repudiation 18s at rank 1, she kites the gaps on Blooming Blows' stacking move speed, and Dream-Laden Bough burns max health while you wait — concede a little and farm toward 6. Then 6 flips it back. Public Execution blinks you to the farthest champion in your line (her, in a 1v1) and suppress-stuns straight through the speed stacks, the one clean answer to a champion who never stands still. Hold it until Swirlseed's flat 12s is spent, then R into Lacerate into Q for the kill. Through first item with Q maxed you out-trade her short combos hard.

edits.before: This is hers if she survives lane. Full-AP Lillia kites you forever with W movement speed and her bouncing E, stacks passive burn faster than you can close, and her long-range R sleep opens fights from outside your dash range. Worse, your damage is entirely physical, so she buys an early Zhonya's or any armor and shrugs off your combo. Your job was to snowball through your 6 and first-item window and end it; if it goes late, group with your team and never chase a low Lillia into fog, because the W speed-up plus a sleep flips the duel instantly.
edits.after: This is hers if she survives lane. Full-AP Lillia kites you forever on Blooming Blows' stacking move speed, burns max health with Dream-Laden Bough, and opens from 1600 range with Lilting Lullaby. That sleep only touches enemies already carrying Dream Dust, so the moment any skill of hers clips you, you become the target — walk out during the drowsy, before it lands. Your damage is entirely physical, so an early Zhonya's or armor blunts the combo. Snowball through 6 and first item and end it; never chase a low Lillia into fog.

edits.after: Blooming Blows costs her nothing to spam at 6s and its edge is true damage MR cannot blunt, while you have one ability — deny last-hits and set up your 2-3 pin.

edits.after: Lacerate's slow into Q-cone and Sundering Slam pins her, and Lillia has no dash in her kit at any level — lead with E, never with Q, and her weak early is yours.

edits.after: Lilting Lullaby needs Dream Dust already on you, and one Blooming Blows tick is enough — from 1600 range her 6 turns any jungler walking top into a free kill.

edits.before: Full-AP Lillia kites with W and her bouncing E and ticks passive burn faster than you can close the gap, and a long-range R sleep opens fights from outside your dash range.

notes: The ambessa/lillia content layer described a Lillia with a W dash, a second E dash and a W shield-slam heal. None of those exist — Riot gives her Dream-Laden Bough, Blooming Blows, Watch Out! Eep!, Swirlseed and Lilting Lullaby, with no dash, no shield and no heal anywhere. The content whys array was also shifted one stage out of alignment with the win array: whys[2] described Levels 4-5, whys[3] described Level 6, whys[4] first item and whys[5] the late game. I re-anchored whys[2] through whys[6] onto the stages they actually label (Level 3, Levels 4-5, Level 6, First item, Two+ items) without touching win[] or any side. Ambessa's kit file flags her W and R as 'grounding' and her R as 'heal' and 'zone'; Riot's descriptions say none of those things, so I made no such claim. Lillia's Swirlseed carries a 'terrain — blocks paths and dashes' flag that her own description contradicts, so I did not claim the seed walls anything off.
